data.narrative:
Helical Fusion, a Series B nuclear energy company founded by Takaya Taguchi and Junichi Miyazawa, is evaluated against a broader nuclear sector comprising 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private competitors including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Aalo Atomics. The company has raised $98M to date.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $98M total raised as a valuation proxy. This yields an implied valuation of $186M. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable given insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear sector; only 4 same-sector peers exist, falling short of the 3+ minimum threshold needed for reliable median-based analysis without introducing sector-wide bias.

The triangulated valuation range is $158M (low) to $214M (high), with a median of $186M. This single-method result should be treated as preliminary pending availability of additional same-stage nuclear or advanced-reactor peers. Key uncertainties include technology differentiation within the helical-fusion design space, path to commercialization timelines relative to competing approaches, and capital intensity of next-stage development. The range reflects stage-typical dilution expectations but lacks peer-corroborating evidence on valuation multiples specific to the helical-fusion subsector.
